children: Oracle's compute capacity for the rest of the year doesn't depend on the company battling through delays and opposition for certain of its flagship data-center projects, KeyBanc Capital Markets analysts write in a note. The company's disclosure that it brought 850 megawatts of capacity online during the first quarter "could not have been better timed with concerns over data center pushback from some key states where Oracle has GW+ sized projects," the analysts write. "The sum of the other projects in flight is able to offset any delays that may be happening and with the increased revenue guidance management clearly feels the capacity roadmap is enough to deliver on its revenue targets this year." (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)
